subject: Mutual action plan: security gating & DPA clarifications for NovaFin eval
messages:
From: Aria Thompson <aria.thompson@novafin.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Lee <michael.lee@novafin.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan & security gating for NovaFin eval

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the demo last week. We want to formalize a short mutual action plan so our Legal and InfoSec teams can clear security gates quickly. Top asks from our side: SOC 2 attestation (scope and date), a SIG/CAIQ mapping or self-assessment, proposed DPA with data residency options, and clarity on data retention (how long logs and data can be kept; ability to set per-environment retention).

High-level timeline we're working to: 4-week technical eval, legal review week 5, decision by week 7. Can you confirm what artifacts you can provide this week and whether Redwood can commit to EU residency for a sandbox environment?

Also tagging Michael (our engineering lead) — he had specific questions about KV cache persistence and whether user content is stored persistently outside ephemeral caches.

Example asks: 
- SOC 2: report + scope, date of most recent audit
- SIG/CAIQ: matrix or answers (we can accept a spreadsheet)
- DPA: we expect standard redlines but will try to narrow to retention/residency
- Retention: default, min configurable, and any cold-archive options

Appreciate a brief MAP (milestones, owners, artifact links) so we can align internal reviewers.

Best,
Aria
Aria Thompson
Head of Cloud Risk, NovaFin

--
Attachment: nova_fin_vendor_questionnaire.pdf (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aria Thompson <aria.thompson@novafin.com>
Cc: Michael Lee <michael.lee@novafin.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & security gating for NovaFin eval

Hi Aria —

Thanks — appreciate the clear asks. We can definitely move quickly. Summary below is the MAP we propose; please tell me if you want any changes to owners or timing.

Proposed MAP (short):
- Week 0 (today): Share SOC 2 summary, SIG/CAIQ mapping, and DPA redline draft — owner: Redwood (me) — ATTACHED
- Week 1: Sandbox access (US + optional EU sandbox) + technical deep-dive with Michael — owner: Redwood Eng (setup by lauren)
- Week 2–3: Evidence review & Q&A (InfoSec/Legal) — owner: NovaFin reviewers / Redwood responders (soojin will help triage)
- Week 4: Closure prep — finalize DPA redlines and retention window; sign intent to proceed
- Week 6–7: Go/no-go decision and contracting cadence

Artifacts we are attaching now: redwood_soc2_summary_v2026.pdf (summary + scope + auditor/date), sig_caiq_mapping_2026.xlsx (spreadsheet mapping answers), proposed_dpa_redlines_2026.docx (trackable redlines focused on residency & retention). Note: the full SOC 2 report is available under NDA; we can initiate a DocSend view or a secure S3 link if your team needs the full report.

On the specific technical points you raised:
- KV cache persistence: Redwood's serving runtime keeps KV caches in-GPU/memory for performance; by default we do not persist user input into long-term storage. Any retention of request/response logs is configurable per-customer and per-deployment.
- Default retention profile options we support today: 30 days (default), 90 days (recommended for production eval), 365 days (long-term). We also support bespoke retention windows for enterprise contracts, and the ability to pin EU residency for hosted or dedicated capacity.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether you need EU sandbox (we can spin up a restricted EU-hosted test in 48–72 hours).
2) Michael — can you propose 60 or 90 minute slots next week for a technical deep-dive?
3) Aria — I'll kick off an NDA if you want the full SOC 2 report access.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary_v2026.pdf; sig_caiq_mapping_2026.xlsx; proposed_dpa_redlines_2026.docx

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Note: if helpful I can produce a compact one-page MAP in Google Doc form and share a link — happy to take that action once Aria confirms owners.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: NovaFin MAP — SOC2 artifacts + SIG triage (action items)

Lauren / Soojin —

Looping you both in to prep for NovaFin. Quick asks from the MAP that we need to cover this week:

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Karthik: Share the three attached artifacts to Aria today (done).
- Lauren: Stand up EU sandbox option and provide provisioning ETA (48–72h) — please confirm whether EU sandbox can be restricted to IP allowlist.
- Soojin: Review sig_caiq_mapping_2026.xlsx and mark any 'partial' answers that require evidence; create an evidence pack (S3 folder) for each partial/NO that InfoSec will request. ETA: Tue EOD.
- Karthik/So0jin: Prepare a 1-pager describing retention configuration (how to set retention per project/environment, where logs are stored, encryption at rest, and deletion mechanics) — want this by Wed morning so I can send to Dana if Legal asks.

Notes: For DPA redlines, Legal usually focuses on residency + subprocessor list + deletion/return obligations. We should mark which subsystems require subprocessor disclosure (analytics, telemetry, optional embeddings store).

Soojin — please prioritize any SIG answers that reference cryptography/keystore (we have KMS integration notes).

Thanks — want to stay on a tight cadence for this one.

Karthik

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: security gating & DPA clarifications for NovaFin eval

Thanks, Karthik — this is helpful and aligns with our internal timing. A few quick notes: 

- We do want an EU sandbox to validate residency and dataflow. Please proceed with provisioning; IP allowlisting would be ideal.
- Legal (Dana) asked that the DPA include a clause for EU residency for sandboxed test data and a proposed retention cap of 180 days for any logs retained during the eval. Can you have your legal team propose a short amendment or confirm your ability to accept 180 days (we can make this a conditional redline in the MAP)?
- Michael will schedule the technical deep-dive next week — he proposes Thu 10:00–11:30 PT or Fri 14:00–15:30 PT; pick which works for your team.

On KV persistence: thanks for the clarification. We will flag any questions that require an architecture sketch — Michael may ask for more detail on how cached keys are evicted and whether any crash-dump path writes to object storage.

Attaching the vendor questionnaire and a short legal intake form. Dana — adding you since you requested the DPA redline.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the artifacts — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Aria
